newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - December 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - December 5.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail:
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Pioneer
INDIA, BANGLADESH TO SIGN WATER PACT

India and Bangladesh are expected to sign a two-year agreement on the contentious issue of sharing Ganga waters early next week during the visit of Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina Wajed. The agreement would ensure a supply of water to Bangladesh during the lean season. The quantum of assured water flow is just a little over the amount specified in a 1977 agreement which lapsed ten years later.
Indian Express
APEX COURT GRANTS SIX YEARS' PAY FOR LAID-OFF WORKERS

The Supreme Court asked the hazardous and polluting units that had been asked to move out of Delhi to pay six years' salary as compensation to the retrenched workers. It also ruled that the polluting units, irrespective of whether they shifted elsewhere or closed down, could use only 32 percent of the land in their possession. The court order came following an appeal by the government seeking protection for the retrenched workers, as a large number of the 168 industries that had been asked to shift out of Delhi filed papers with the Labour Commissioner for closure.
The Hindustan Times
OVER 300,000 SHIFTED TO SAFE AREAS AS HURRICAN NEARS

Over 300,000 people living in low-lying villages and hamlets in coastal Andhra Pradesh, identified as most vulnerable to cyclones, were shifted to safe areas as a cyclone threatened to hit the eastern coast. Contrary to earlier predictions, the cyclone was moving at a reduced pace toward the coast. The cyclone may hit the coast in the wee hours of Thursday.
The Economic Times
INSURANCE REGULATORY BODY MAY GET LICENSING POWERS

The government is planning to delegate powers to the Insurance Regulatory Authority (IRA) to issue licences to private Indian and foreign insurance companies wishing to set up shop in India. This is despite protests by the left-wing sections of the government against the move. A draft IRA bill containing the licensing provision, among a host of other guidelines outlining the role of the IRA, is believed to be ready and awaiting cabinet nod. Sources said the government is keen to introduce the bill in the current session of parliament, and if that is not possible, then during the budget session.
MEET TO DISCUSS SLUGGISH MARKET CONDITIONS

Top Finance Ministry officials are to meet the chiefs of the three major investment financial institutions (FIs) to review the prevailing sluggish market conditions. The exact agenda of the meeting is not known. However, market sources said the current market situation was likely to figure prominently in the meeting. The meeting assumes significance in view of the finance minister's recent call to FIs to take more risks in the secondary market.
RELIANCE KEEPS OFF ROAMING CONSORTIA

Reliance Telecom Ltd, the company with seven cellular licences, has chosen not to join any of the roaming consortiums. All other cellular operators in the country have split into two camps. While nine operators have formed the World1 Network, seven others are forming the Global Connect Network to allow roaming facility to their subscribers. Reliance, which has the circles of Madhya Pradesh, Bihar, Orissa, West Bengal, Assam, North East and Himachal Pradesh, is adopting a wait and watch attitude, as it knows that all of India cannot be covered by either of the roaming consortia without its presence.
ALUMINIUM MAJORS HIT BY RISING COSTS

Aluminium companies were hit by various problems in the first half of fiscal 1996/97 (April-March). Indian Aluminium Company Ltd' (Indal) profits fell owing to problems with its extrusions division, coupled with rising raw material costs. Indal's net profit plummeted by 20.84 percent to 382.1 million rupees from 482.7 million rupees. Rising administered prices of inputs like petro-products, power and coal caused a downfall in the margins of aluminium companies. A decline in the global prices of alumina and aluminium was also responsible for the falling margins. Power cuts were a major worry. Financial Express
DEMAND FOR BASIC SERVICES LICENCE REVIEW REJECTED

The Law Ministry turned down the demand of prospective basic telecommunication service operators to review the licence agreement's contentious clauses, including assignability of licences. Sources said the contentious issues had been referred by the Communications Ministry to the Law Ministry in the wake of the stalemate between private industry and the Department of Telecommunications (DoT). The private operators had been demanding assignability on the grounds that it would facilitate raising of much-needed funds for the sector, facing an acute resource crunch. Sources said the law ministry decision might jeopardise the privatisation of basic services.
RUPEE FALLS ON HEAVY DOLLAR BUYING

The rupee hit the 35.85 dollar level on Wednesday after the previous close of 35.73 in active trading in the interbank foreign exchange market. Dealers said both the Reserve Bank of India and the State Bank of India (SBI) made heavy purchases in the dollar during the day. SBI purchase was prompted by the dollar requirement of its public sector clients like Indian Oil and Oil and Natural Gas Corporation, market sources said.
BOMBAY BOURSE INDEX PLUNGES TO 2713 POINTS

Stock prices declined as selling pressure on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) pushed the sensitive index to an intra-day low of 2713.12. It closed slightly higher at 2745.06, down 52.94 points from the previous close of 2798.00. The National Stock Exchange-50 fell by 21.28 points from its overnight close of 809.43. Prices slid heavily in the global depository market (GDR) market. The Skindia GDR Index lost 2.49 percent to close at an all-time low of 54.10. Panic selling continued with little institutional support. The cement sector was the worst hit, with the GDRs falling 14.39 percent. The auto-sector GDRs declined 10.49 percent, power 8.14 percent, steel 7.14 percent, aluminium 7.02 per
SIMOCO EYES BRITISH, AUSTRALIAN MARKETS

British-based Simoco International's sister concern Simoco India hopes to start exporting radio base stations to Britain and Australia from the middle of next year. Simoco entered the telecommunications manufacturing sector after its worldwide takeover of Philips' Private Mobile Radio division (PMR). Now, 70 percent of Simoco is held by UK-based CIN Ven, a capital venture group with $45 billion worth funds. Simoco has gained control of the Calcutta-based Philips Telecom (India) Ltd. It has applied to the government to get a majority stake in this company.
BANKS' DEALS WITH SUBSIDIARIES MAY BE BARRED

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI), the central bank, is likely to bar commercial banks from entering into any financial transactions with their subsidiaries. The central bank also might stop the prevailing system of direct inspection of subsidiaries by the promoter-banks. The RBI move assumes significance in the context of the poor performance of these subsidiaries, resulting in their bailout by the parent banks. The central bank's move is based on the recommendations of the RBI working group set up to review the internal control and inspection system in banks.
Business Standard
GDR MARKET CAPITALISATION DOWN 39 PCT

There has been a hefty erosion in market capitalisation of 39.26 percent for Indian Global Depository Receipts (GDRs) in the past six months. This was revealed by a latest study conducted by Skindia Finance. The study showed market capitalisation for India GDR offerings fell from $4,541 million on June 4 to $2,758 million on December 4. Analysts said, with India GDR markets following the local market trends, foreign investors' confidence had taken a beating and trading sentiment was at its lowest levels. Market operators ruled out a recovery of the GDR markets without fresh buying interest on local bourses.
MINISTRY FAVOURS ONLY PARTIAL BID REGULATION OF COAL

The Chari committee report suggesting complete deregulation of the coal industry has been put on the back burner following opposition from the coal ministry. A ministry spokesman said the report was still under ministry consideration. But sources said senior ministry officials were opposed to the idea of total decontrol and favoured partial deregulation. The Chari committee was set up the Planning Commission to formulate an integrated coal policy for adoption by the government during the ninth and 10th five-year plans.
The Observer
MINISTRY TO BOOST COAL-BASED POWER PROJECTS

The power ministry plans to encourage coal-based mega power projects with a capacity ranging from 1,000 mw and above as part of a long-term energy policy. The ministry course was due to the government having limited options to go in for nuclear, hydro and liquid fuel-based power projects. According to the power ministry, nuclear and the hydro-based mega power projects in India were not viable due to various secio-economic factors. The liquid fuel-based projects could not be encouraged due to non-availability of raw material at home. PLAN TO EXPAND AUTOMATIC FOREIGN INVESTMENT LIST REVIVED

The industry ministry has called for further liberalisation of foreign direct investment (FDI) by expanding the automatic approval list of industries permitting foreign equity up to 51 percent. The step was earlier deferred by cabinet following opposition by the Left parties and the agriculture minister. The industry ministry's cabinet note proposes to extend the automatic approval list to include the industries of power, surface transport, port, automobiles, mining, chemicals, food processing, water distribution/supply and consultancy services. It calls for raising the limit on foreign stake from the existing 51 percent to 74 percent for approvals through the automatic route.
